title: Addison's disease: causes and hormone-deficiency features
guide: 1° = Addison's; 2° (m/c) = abrupt steroid withdrawal, pituitary/hypothalamic dysfunction. Causes: autoimmune m/c (PGA/APS 1&2, anti-21-OH antibody; isolated adrenalitis); inherited — Aladin (3A/4A: alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, ANS), X-ALD (↑VLCFA), T-pit (corticotrophs only); infective — TB m/c in India, meningococcaemia → Waterhouse-Friderichsen. Glands enlarged/normal/atrophic/asymmetrical. GC↓: asthenia, anorexia, weight loss, hypoglycaemia, euvolemic hyponatremia, eosinophilia; MC↓: hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt craving, ↑BUN/Cr; SS↓: dry skin, lost axillary/pubic hair, lost libido; ACTH↑: hyperpigmentation 90% (sun-exposed, oral mucosa); plus normocytic anemia and hypercalcaemia → auricular calcification (adrenal calcification absent).

title: Crisis, 1° vs 2° differences and the cortisol/Synacthen work-up
guide: Crisis precipitants: infection/any stress, abrupt steroid withdrawal; features acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia, hypotension/circulatory failure; Rx fluids + steroids. 1° vs 2°: MC ↓ vs normal; ACTH ↑ vs ↓; pigmentation, salt craving/postural hypotension, vitiligo + vs −; K+ ↑ vs normal; Na+ ↓↓ both. Fasting cortisol <3 = Addison's, >20 rules out, 3–20 → Synacthen 250 µg IM/IV, peak <18 confirms, >18 rules out.

title: Replacement therapy: maintenance, equivalence and crisis protocol
guide: Maintenance oral hydrocortisone DOC 20 mg/day (10+5+5); prednisolone/dexamethasone alternatives; fludrocortisone 50–100 µg if MC deficiency. Fever/infection double dose; hospitalisation 50–75 mg/day; surgery day 50–100 mg IV. Equivalence 0.75 dexa = 4 methylpred = 5 prednisolone = 20 hydrocortisone = 25 cortisol. Crisis: 100 mg IV stat + 50 mg Q6H (day 1 = 300 mg), 200/100/50 mg days 2–4, oral 25 mg (10,10,5) ×1 week → 20 mg (10,5,5) ± fludrocortisone; fluids NS/DNS 1 L over 1 h then 2–3 L over 12 h.
